options.architecture: Core enumerates every complete legal damage allocation and controller selects one opaque option.
options.correctness: Potentially correct if exhaustive and validated.
options.integration_impact: Simple provider surface but large payloads.
options.performance: Poor in high power / many recipient cases; complete integer allocation space is combinatorial.

options.architecture: Controller proposes arbitrary map; core only validates final map.
options.correctness: Better than current but external pilot/provider still has to invent candidate allocations and therefore risks reconstructing Magic legality to find a valid proposal.

options.architecture: Core creates an immutable/transactional damage-assignment decision for one assigning player in one damage step, exposes only core-derived next recipients/allowed integer ranges or legal amount candidates, and independently validates the complete transaction before commit.
options.complexity: Bounded but nontrivial: new combat-core decision/validator classes plus migration of human GUI/AI/controller callback.
options.correctness: Strong; handles CR 510.1e total-assignment legality and CR 702.19 same-step cross-source lethal accounting without pilot rules.
options.integration_impact: Headless-friendly; GUI, AI and external provider consume same rules surface.
options.upstreamability: Moderate-high because it removes duplicated GUI/AI legality and gives tests a single authority.

options.architecture: Commander Lab/provider computes legal allocations from Forge state.
options.correctness: Violates mandatory architecture; creates second rules engine.
